run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 14 of the usual 15 holdings. Mastercard wasn't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the company itself.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris is flat today, and the real story is that its profit on each dollar of sales still runs below the other big defense contractors, which is why the stock hasn't bounced back the way theirs have even after a steep fall.

ASML.sentence: ASML slipped a couple percent and is now down about a fifth from its high, which is unusual for a company that only ever grinds upward — they're still the only firm on earth making a certain essential chipmaking machine, so this is a rare dip rather than a changed story.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet week — industrial gas demand is steady, their contracts are long-term, and they nudge prices up a little each quarter, which is pretty much the whole story.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is holding up better than the other AI names during this pullback — the cloud-and-AI story keeps grinding along without any real drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is sitting near its highs and barely moved — nothing much is happening, which is fine for a company that just sells the equipment every lab needs.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is flat today; oil is unusually high right now because fighting involving Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments, so the fat profits are coming from the oil price rather than anything Chevron did — at the ordinary oil price they plan around, the picture is more modest.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen by half from its high and looks badly beaten down, even though companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow-automation and AI-assistant tools on long multi-year contracts — so the drop is about mood, not the business.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore dropped more than 5% even as copper prices surged, an odd gap given that mining and trading copper is a big part of what they do — the stock may just be lagging the metal.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta slipped a bit, but the price it actually gets per ton of crushed rock is still creeping up around 3-4%, which is the part that matters — their quarries each own a patch of the map nobody else can economically serve.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA dipped mainly because the Mexican peso weakened against the dollar, which trims the value of this Latin American Coke bottler's earnings when they're converted back — more a currency move than a business one.

UBER.sentence: Uber fell nearly 5%, but people keep booking more rides and food orders than ever — bookings for its rides business grew about 20% last quarter — so this is a wobble in a business that's still clearly growing, not a problem with it.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is roughly flat, and its shares are priced below what it would cost to replace its fleet of ships — a classic bargain signal in container shipping, though trade conditions set the pace here.

MA.sentence: Mastercard didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot company is down about a third from its high and lagging other medical-device makers, but there's no sign hospitals are using its machines less, so it reads as fear rather than a real loss of business.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia is down sharply along with the other AI names after Google's parent and Amazon showed they're now borrowing to pay for all the computing gear they buy — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are the customers who pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
